messages:
Priya (Product): Quick thread to lock down GA scope for private deploy. I want clear, customer-facing buckets and a tiny network contract so field can sell without overpromising.

Ethan (Eng): Agreed. We should avoid 'we do everything' language. Propose three tiers: Core GA, Network-Stable, Compliance-Ready.

Liam (Field): Field asks: include what we *dont* cover in Core GA. Biggest upset is when customers expect BGP/peering on day 0.

Priya (Product): Draft Core GA bullets: single-node operator, offline installer tar + signed manifest, self-signed certs default, documented minor-upgrade lane that keeps PVs and service names, no customer LB required.

Rosa (Infra): For the signed manifest we need a key rotation note. Ops can stand up signing service but its a dependency. I'll add a TODO to infra backlog.

Noah (PM): Network-Stable bullets please? We need to describe exactly what static IP / LB support looks like. Sales will ask for SLA language.

Ethan (Eng): Network-Stable: multi-node HA operator, installer accepts a static VIP/IP in values.yaml, installer emits a "network-contract" YAML that the customer applies (contains LB type, VIP, cert mode). Installer validates reachability and stores a hash for upgrade verification.

Liam (Field): Love the network-contract idea. Field will require the contract to include a contactable netops owner on the customer side and a test curl endpoint for smoke validation.

Priya (Product): Compliance-Ready = everything in Network-Stable + KMS BYOK, audit log export, configurables for retention, and a security review gate. This will be commercial/enterprise-only.

Rosa (Infra): Technical constraint: preserving VIP across upgrades on certain CNI providers is flaky. We should call out supported CNIs for Network-Stable and provide a fallback doc.

Ethan (Eng): Implementation note: to preserve IP we reuse the Service object by setting metadata.annotations from the network-contract and refuse to replace it if the hash matches. If the contract changes we fail upgrade and emit clear remediation steps.

Liam (Field): Please include a clear customer-facing sentence: "If you change the network contract (VIP, LB type), an upgrade may require a maintenance window." Sales needs that.

Noah (PM): Prioritization ask: which parts start now? I vote Core GA + network-contract schema and static VIP plumbing in parallel. That unblocks 3 pilots.

Ethan (Eng): Rough ETA: Core GA ~5w (1x eng + docs), network-contract + validator + VIP plumbing ~3w if we parallelize with a second eng. Compliance-Ready TBD after GA.

Rosa (Infra): Infra tasks this sprint: create signing key + publish public key, add simple KMS shim for later BYOK. Ops-bot: confirm build queue.

infra-bot: ci: installer build queued (build-2026.04.02-0920).

Priya (Product): Decision: ship Core GA with explicit exclusions documented; start network-contract and VIP plumbing immediately; leave Compliance-Ready for roadmap cycle. Owners: Ethan = Core GA lead, Liam = network-contract spec + validation owner, Rosa = infra signing + KMS shim, Noah = sales one-pager.

Liam (Field): I'll draft network-contract YAML template by EOD tomorrow and include the netops contact field and smoke endpoint.

Ethan (Eng): I'll open tickets for upgrade-lane preservation and validator. Need acceptance tests: smoke test that verifies VIP preserved across a patch upgrade.

Noah (PM): I'll draft the customer one-pager and a short FAQ: "What we don't do in Core GA" + upgrade expectations + support tiers.

Rosa (Infra): Ops note: require customers to provide a reachable DNS name or IP for VIP validation, otherwise installer will warn and continue in a non-VIP mode.

Priya (Product): Perfect. We'll review status in Friday sync. Small, conservative GA, with a concrete path to Network-Stable. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
